blurb: Large southern African hound with a ridge of hair growing backwards along its spine
description: The Rhodesian Ridgeback is a large hound from southern Africa with a short wheaten coat and a reversed ridge of hair, described as dignified.
answer: The Rhodesian Ridgeback is a large dog breed from southern Africa, standardized in Bulawayo in what is now Zimbabwe in 1922. It is muscular, with a short light-to-red wheaten coat and a distinctive ridge of hair growing in the opposite direction along its back, and is described as dignified and intelligent.

body: Its forebears include the ridged hunting and guard dogs of the Khoikhoi, which early Cape colonists crossed with European breeds to produce Boer hunting dogs. In the late nineteenth century the hunter Cornelius van Rooyen developed a line able to bay lions, harassing the animal until the hunter could shoot it. F. R. Barnes drafted the first standard in 1922, the South African Kennel Union approved it in 1927, and the American Kennel Club recognized the breed in 1955 as a hound.

The ridge is a fan-shaped band formed by two whorls, or crowns, tapering from behind the shoulders to the hips. Under the FCI standard males stand 64–69 cm and weigh about 36.5 kg, with females somewhat smaller. The coat is short, dense, sleek and glossy, light wheaten to red wheaten, with white allowed on the chest and toes. The nose is black or liver, with eye color matching.

The FCI standard describes the breed as dignified and intelligent, and the UKC standard says it can be aloof with strangers but never shy or aggressive. The author of the first standard warned that the dogs respond poorly to rough handling, and the breed is said to accept fair correction from people it trusts.
Sources give little detail on daily exercise or grooming. As a large, athletic hound bred for hunting, it is generally expected to need regular activity; the short coat is described as low in bulk.

Conditions reported in the breed include hip dysplasia, dermoid sinus, hypothyroidism, degenerative myelopathy and gastric dilatation volvulus (bloat). The US breed club recommends screening breeding dogs for hips, elbows, thyroid and eyes. A UK study found an average life expectancy of 12 years.

faq.q: How big does a Rhodesian Ridgeback get?
faq.a: Ridgebacks typically stand about 61–69 cm at the withers and weigh roughly 32–37 kg.

faq.q: Do all Rhodesian Ridgebacks have a ridge?
faq.a: No. The ridge comes from a dominant mutation, and some purebred puppies are born without one; ridgelessness is the only disqualification in the AKC standard.

faq.q: How long do Rhodesian Ridgebacks live?
faq.a: A UK study found an average life expectancy of 12 years.

faq.q: Is the Rhodesian Ridgeback recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 146 in Group 6, scent hounds and related breeds.
